subject.title: Make adaptive refresh agent-aware with explicit local activity consent

question: Should CodexBar make Adaptive the fresh-install default and accept that indistinguishable configless legacy installs will also move to Adaptive, or should agent-aware Adaptive remain an explicitly selected mode?
rationale: Source and runtime evidence can validate implementation behavior, but only the repository owner can accept the new default, the unavoidable legacy-cohort behavior change, and the local process/session inspection contract.

options.title: Keep Adaptive explicitly selected
options.body: Retain the five-minute default for unmarked installs and prompt for local activity only when a user explicitly selects Adaptive.

options.title: Approve the new default
options.body: Accept Adaptive for fresh and indistinguishable legacy installs, with the disclosed consent-gated process and session scan.

options.title: Pause the default change
options.body: Retain the scanner and proof work for a narrower future proposal after broader product evidence or reliable install-origin signaling exists.

recommendation.title: Keep Adaptive explicitly selected
recommendation.body: Retain the five-minute default for unmarked installs and prompt for local activity only when a user explicitly selects Adaptive.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced Agent Sessions and its default-off privacy boundary and are the clearest owner of the competing refresh-default and local-scanning policies.
